classification.habit: Small to medium thorny deciduous tree
classification.habitat: Dry deciduous forests, scrub and open woodland
classification.distribution: Widespread in the Indian subcontinent, especially drier regions

identification.description: A thorny tree with bipinnate leaves, small pale flowers in spikes and brown flat pods; heartwood is characteristically dark and rich in tannins.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium deciduous tree with spreading crown.
identification.stem: Branching woody stem often armed with paired spines; mature bark grey-brown.
identification.leaf: Small bipinnate leaves with many tiny leaflets and prominent stipular spines on young branches.
identification.flower: Small pale flowers in cylindrical spikes.
identification.fruit: Flat, thin, brown legume pod with several seeds.
identification.seed: Small flattened seeds within the pod.
identification.bark: Grey-brown rough bark; heartwood is darker and traditionally used as the principal drug material in this record.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Khadira heartwood is rich in tannins and catechin-type constituents; exact marker values should be taken from authenticated pharmacopoeial material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Senegalia catechu is a tannin-rich tree used traditionally for astringent preparations. Modern evidence should be linked to the specific preparation and indication.
modern_information.safety_notes: Avoid assuming that heartwood, bark and commercial catechu extracts are chemically identical.

exam_points: Heartwood is the listed useful part
mnemonics: Khadira = Khair: thorns + bipinnate leaves + dark heartwood.
student.quick_revision: Khadira is a thorny Senegalia tree; heartwood is the listed drug and is characteristically tannin-rich.

teaching_points: Demonstrate Fabaceae leaf and fruit characters and crude heartwood identification.
discussion_points: Difference between crude heartwood and catechu extracts
practical_points: Observe spines, bipinnate leaves, pods and heartwood colour.

doctor.quick_reference: Khadira — Senegalia catechu; heartwood listed as useful in this project record.
key_precautions: Authenticate heartwood and distinguish it from bark.
Verify dose and formulation from authoritative references.
